summary: John Claude White worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School in 1868 and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876), later serving as an Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, John Clifford Holt studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He was Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978–2017) and held posts at Calgary and Chicago.

An indologist and linguist, John Collinson Nesfield studied at Highgate School and Merton College. He taught at Highgate, held professorships at Presidency University and Krishnagar Government College, served as principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878), and became an Allahabad Fellow (1887).

A religious studies scholar, John Corrigan completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). His career includes positions at the University of Virginia, Arizona State University, and Florida State University, where he chaired the Department of Religion around 2001.

John Crawfurd was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803). He worked as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808) and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
John Cripps Pembrey was an indologist and linguist. He served as Oriental Reader at the Clarendon Press, attested in both 1904 and 1916.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, John D. Dunne studied at Amherst College, CIHTS, and Harvard University (Ph.D.). He held posts at CIHTS, Emory University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison as Distinguished Chair in Contemplative Humanities (1999).

An indologist and historian/archaeologist, John D. Kelly serves at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007 and attested in 2026 as Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

John D. Smith is an indologist and linguist. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) before joining the University of Cambridge, where he was University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1984) and Professor (2001–2007).

A Buddhist studies figure who studied under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi, Loori taught at Naropa University in 1974. He founded the Mountains and Rivers Order and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from ~1980 until 2009.
A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, John Daishin Buksbazen studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman (attested 2002).

A linguist and sinologist, John DeFrancis studied at Yale University (~1933–1936) and Columbia University (~1941–1948). He later held academic posts at Seton Hall University (~1964–1966) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1976).

Philosopher John Dewey studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1884–1894), University of Minnesota, University of Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

An indologist and linguist who studied under Edwin Norris, John Dowson tutored at East India Company College (~1855–1858) and served as Professor of Hindustani at Staff College, Camberley and University College London (1855–1877).

John E. Cort is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and his AM at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Denison University from ~1993 to 2021.

John F. Richards was an indologist and historian who studied at the University of New Hampshire and UC Berkeley. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

An indologist and historian, Fleet studied at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), as Epigraphist to the Government of India (1883–1886), and as Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1906).
John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from ~1876 to 1902 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from ~1891 to 1903.

An indologist and religious studies scholar, John George Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford, and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He was a Calcutta High Court Judge (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).

A linguist and Central Asian specialist, Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, and Indiana University Bloomington (full professor 1965–1989), and founded The Mongolia Society in 1961.
